protectedRevelations: Institutional design prescriptions and decentralized-brand operational rules

scenes.title: The founders we do not hear about
scenes.viewerPurpose: Notice the capable builders missing from famous success stories Ask what those favorite stories leave out Recognize effort alongside factors outside one person’s control
addOrChange: Add a modest second workbench in the distance; remove the prestige profile so the worker stays central.

cues.narration: For every celebrated founder, many capable people spend years building something the world barely notices.
cues.visualAction: Reveal the completed chair and the maker waiting beside several dated work notes.

cues.narration: The Founder Lottery asks what our favorite success stories leave out.
cues.visualAction: Let the second, equally careful workbench come into view as the film title is introduced.

cues.narration: Skill matters, but effort does not control timing, access, or the attention of a market.
cues.visualAction: Keep both products unchanged while an empty visitor space makes the uncertainty of attention visible.

scenes.title: Faster tools, harder attention
scenes.viewerPurpose: See AI helping a team and all its competitors Notice trust becoming harder while building gets easier
scenes.composition: Two comparable chairs and one customer, with an identical design tool beside each.
addOrChange: Add a second copy of the design tool; replace question-icon emphasis with the customer examining build history.

cues.narration: AI gives small teams remarkable tools while giving their competitors the same advantage.
cues.visualAction: Give both makers the same small design tool at the same time.

cues.narration: Making a product gets easier; getting people to trust it may not.
cues.visualAction: The customer turns from the finished surfaces to the repair and service history.

scenes.title: Sharing the cost of starting
scenes.viewerPurpose: Care about useful work that receives no applause Imagine sharing support while keeping independence Ask who earns credit and carries the cost
scenes.composition: Two independent workshops share a readable name and one contribution record.
addOrChange: Reduce the registry to three visible entries: contribution, obligation and exit; leave ownership questions unfilled.

cues.narration: The book follows that pressure through ambition, collaboration, and the work nobody applauds.
cues.visualAction: Show a small repair recorded alongside the two operators, giving maintenance equal visual weight.

cues.narration: Could builders share tools and a trusted name while still choosing their own work?
cues.visualAction: Place the shared name between the workshops without enclosing either workshop.

cues.narration: That raises harder questions about who earns credit, who pays, and who can leave.
cues.visualAction: One operator holds a portable copy of the record while both review the unanswered obligations.

scenes.title: Another kind of venture
scenes.viewerPurpose: Connect the question to wanting to make something useful Wonder whether ambition could become less lonely
scenes.composition: An open book and an ordinary chair joint on a reader’s table.
addOrChange: Use one short reading tab for the shared-infrastructure discussion; remove any growth or valuation imagery.

cues.narration: For anyone who wants to create something useful, the question reaches beyond another startup pitch.
cues.visualAction: The reader compares the practical joint with the book’s discussion.

cues.narration: Could we make the experiment less lonely without making the ambition smaller?
cues.visualAction: End with room for a second reader beside the table, an invitation to shared work.
